target_customer: Households buying a home chore humanoid robot
problem: Humanoid robots are made by hundreds per year because motors are expensive and slow to assemble, so they cannot reach homes at consumer prices.
business_model: Consumer hardware sales (target price comparable to an iPhone)
product_category: Humanoid home robot using artificial muscles

founders.name: Richard Gong
education: Dropped out of medicine at Oxford (per YC page)
founders.background_notes: Previously built AI systems for personalized cancer vaccines (per YC page)

founders.name: Chenny (Qianyi) Deng
education: PhD candidate in Computer Science, Oxford (per YC page; one profile says she left)

technical_complexity.rationale: Building a humanoid with hydraulic style braided artificial muscles and a single pump, 22 DoF hands and a sub-$1000 claimed prototype is hardware research grade, though the team claims a prototype in two months.

defensibility.rationale: Custom artificial muscle design could be proprietary, but no patents or independent validation were found and robotics rivals are well funded.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Home humanoid players were pre-selling or building at the time; no source shows an effect on Piggy.

market_need_then: Home humanoid interest was high in 2025 with 1X NEO pre-orders at $20,000 reported in later coverage; demand for a cheaper robot is asserted by the company, not shown.

identity.visual_style: Minimal landing page, tagline humanoid robots for the home
identity.voice_and_tone: Friendly, consumer facing, low price promise (iPhone prices)

brand_strength.rationale: Playful name but no press or community evidence found.

outcome_analysis: Piggy Robotics is a very young Fall 2025 YC company claiming a sub-$1000 artificial muscle humanoid prototype built in two months. No independent coverage, shutdown or acquisition was found, so there is no outcome to analyze yet; the hardware scaling claim is unverified and a Russian outlet questioned scalability.
notes: VCBacked lists $500K pre-seed in Dec 2025 from YC and Pioneer Fund; single aggregator so unverified and not recorded as a round. Founded year not stated by sources (one profile says 2024, unverified). Team size is 5 on YC profile, launch post says 16 engineers. Competitor search returned only coverage dated 2026, so list left empty. Completeness pass: the 500K pre-seed dated 2025-12 rests on databases (VCBacked, Preqin calls it seed); no press confirmation.
